summary: Backend-only validation of the NEW /api/transfers module + extended Income/Expense optional fields. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_transfers_api.py with 14 pytest tests organized in 6 classes. Coverage: (1) TransferCreate happy path returns transfer_id (prefix 'txfr_'), type='transfer', amount=5000, and atomically debits from_account (50000→45000) / credits to_account (10000→15000); (2) validations: amount=0 → 422, amount=-100 → 422, from==to → 400 with 'different' in detail, missing account ids → 422, unknown/other-user account → 404; (3) GET list — created 3 back-to-back transfers and all 3 show in the listing (validates the firebase_config.insert_one 'transfer_id' preference-list fix for multi-record persistence in SINGLE_USER_DOC_COLLECTIONS path); (4) GET one — 404 for non-existent id; (5) PUT amount 5000→7000: verified _balance(from) 50000→43000 and _balance(to) 10000→17000 (old impact reversed, new applied); (6) PUT from_account_id swap: a1→a3 move on a 4000 transfer correctly reverts a1 to 50000, debits a3 20000→16000, leaves to-account a2 untouched at 14000; (7) DELETE reverses balances back to baseline and subsequent GET returns 404; (8) DASHBOARD isolation — current-month transfer does NOT move monthly_income/monthly_expenses AND total_balance stays conserved (inter-account move); (9) Income POST with labels=['salary','base'], location='Office', attachment_url → all round-trip via GET /api/income; (10) Expense POST with labels+payee='Amazon'+location+attachment_url → all round-trip via GET /api/expenses. Regressions: legacy /app/balance_fix_test.py ✅, /app/deploy_verify_multirecord.py ✅, and FULL pytest suite (109/109 = 95 existing + 14 new) passes in 449s. No backend issues found.

minor.issue: Error message for from==to on UPDATE uses 'must differ' while CREATE uses 'must be different'. Minor copy inconsistency; both are 400. Non-blocking.
No pagination cursor; `limit` hard-caps at 1000. Fine for current scale, flag for future.

Transfer balance adjustments are NOT wrapped in a Firestore transaction — if insert_one succeeds but the second _adjust_balance throws mid-way, balances can drift. In practice both calls are near-guaranteed succeed together, but a server crash between the two $inc calls would leave state inconsistent. Consider wrapping in db.run_transaction or at least adding a rollback try/except. Non-blocking for single-user MVP.

action_items: (Optional) Harmonize the 400 error detail string for from==to across CREATE ('must be different') and UPDATE ('must differ').
(Optional, future hardening) Wrap the two _adjust_balance calls in POST/PUT/DELETE /api/transfers inside a Firestore transaction or add an explicit rollback on partial failure.
critical_code_review_comments: transfers.py is well-scoped (~217 lines), clean separation from server.py via late-import of get_current_user. Good module boundary — matches the pattern used by snapshots.py.
TransferCreate uses Pydantic Field(gt=0) correctly for amount validation → 422 at the schema layer before any DB hit.
_adjust_balance uses MongoDB-style $inc with $set updated_at → same atomic pattern that fixed the earlier balance_fix regression. Re-use of that pattern is correct.
UPDATE path correctly reverses OLD impact (+old.amount to from, -old.amount to to) then applies NEW impact — the full 4-leg rebalance verified by test_change_from_account_rebalances.
Transfer docs are excluded from dashboard income/expense aggregation because /api/dashboard only queries db.income and db.expenses, never db.transfers — verified by TestDashboardTransferIsolation.

firebase_config.insert_one preference list correctly includes 'transfer_id' BEFORE user_id so doc-id matches transfer_id and multiple transfers don't collide under single-user mode (SINGLE_USER_DOC_COLLECTIONS allowlist). Multi-record test confirms 3 concurrent inserts all persist.
Income & Expense extended models (labels, payee [expense only], location, attachment_url) persist and round-trip correctly via both POST response and GET listing.
Minor: _parse_iso raises 400 but uses a non-standard error shape {detail: 'Invalid date format: ...'} — consistent with FastAPI default HTTPException, OK.
Minor: balance mutations are not transactional. In production Firestore you could use db.run_transaction() or a compensating-write pattern; the MVP-level exposure is acceptable but worth tracking.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Transfer module is fully covered by /app/backend/tests/test_transfers_api.py. Key invariants to preserve when extending: (a) transfers are NEVER aggregated by /api/dashboard's monthly_income/monthly_expenses — they live only in db.transfers collection; (b) create/update/delete must atomically adjust BOTH account balances via _adjust_balance with $inc; (c) firebase_config.insert_one preference list must include any new per-record id field (now: income_id, expense_id, bill_id, card_id, investment_id, heading_id, loan_id, lending_id, rental_id, reminder_id, note_id, family_member_id, goal_id, budget_id, account_id, transfer_id) BEFORE user_id. Full regression (109 tests) takes ~7.5min; use --junitxml for reporting. Backend URL: https://cash-flow-hub-81.preview.emergentagent.com/api.
